description: A cited research brief on a question, built by reading free public sources (Wikipedia, arXiv, Crossref, OpenAlex, any URL you name or documents you paste) and quoting them verbatim with a numbered citation per claim. Delivered as brief.md, sources.json and an evidence.json ledger that classifies every statement, with every quotation checked against the source it cites. Choose this when you need a short, checkable briefing on a question and you would rather have verbatim quotations with working citations than a paraphrase you cannot verify. It also works with no network access at all: paste your own source documents and the brief is built from them. Do not choose this for a synthesised argument across sources, for a general web search index (it reads Wikipedia, arXiv, Crossref and OpenAlex, plus any URL or document you supply), or for anything that must be behind a login. Example requests: Research how x402 payments settle on Base and give me a brief with sources I can check. | I need a cited briefing on a topic, with every claim linked to the page it came from. | Read these two vendor documents I pasted and tell me where they disagree.

accepted_price.description: The amount accepted, exactly as quoted (for example "5.00" or 5). Checked against the stored quote, so a price that moved between quote and authorize is refused rather than silently absorbed. Optional, but sent to make the acceptance explicit.

authorized_by.description: Identifier of the human or agent authorizing this job.

idempotency_key.description: Retry key. Re-sending the same key returns the same job instead of running it twice.

documents.description: Optional: your own source material, for when the topic is not in the free corpus or you want a brief built only from what you supply. Start each document with a header line '--- document: <label>' and optionally '; published: <YYYY-MM-DD>' on the same line, then the text (at most 5 documents). When this is present the free corpus is not searched and no network access is used.

max_sources.description: How many sources to read, 2 to 8 (default 4).

question.description: The research question, in one or two sentences.

sources.description: Optional: extra http(s) URLs to read alongside the free corpus, comma or space separated (at most 5).

payment_signature.description: Base64-encoded x402 payment payload (the value the HTTP interface puts in the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header), signed for the amount in the payment requirement the first call returned. Required for a priced capability; nothing is charged until the work completes.

quote_id.description: The quote_id returned by POST /v1/jobs. Required to authorize a priced capability; the service rejects a priced job that does not name the quote it issued.

name: submit_web_research_brief

access_token.description: Per-job credential. Present it as the X-Job-Token header to read the job or list it. Keep it; it is the only credential for this job.

verification.description: Independent verification. verification.ok = false means the job failed, not a partial success.

title: Web Research Brief
